title: Two Hamzahs in Two Words - when both hamzahs carry kasrah: إِ إِ
titleEn: Two Hamzahs in Two Words - when both hamzahs carry kasrah: إِ إِ

isqat_of_the_first_hamzah.title: Isqāṭ/ḥadhf of the 1st
isqat_of_the_first_hamzah.description: Isqāṭ/ḥadhf (dropping) of the 1st of the two hamzahs. For example the first hamzah in بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا is dropped and this is read: بِالسُّو إِلَّا
isqat_of_the_first_hamzah.note: Imam al-Shaṭibī in line 202 mentions it is the first hamzah that is dropped. This then implies that the now present madd is a madd munfaṣil and would be read with the either qaṣr or tawassuṯ in accordance with the rules of munfaṣil for these qurra. However there are some scholars that said it is in fact the second hamzah that will be dropped, thereby making the madd a madd muttaṣil. The former opinion is the preferred opinion of most scholars.

tashil_of_first.title: Tashῑl of 1st
tashil_of_first.description: Tashῑl of 1st means to recite the first of the two hamzahs with a blend of the long vowel yāʾ and the second clearly (taḥqīq).
tashil_of_first.note: Both qaṣr and tawassuṯ are allowed.

tashil_of_second.title: Tashῑl of 2nd
tashil_of_second.description: Tashῑl of 2nd means to recite the first of the two hamzahs clearly (taḥqīq) and recite the second hamzah with a blend of the long vowel yāʾ.
tashil_of_second.note: This is one of two options for both Imams Warsh and Qunbul

ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_ya_sakinah.title: Ibdāl of 2nd to yā sākinah (يْ)
ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_ya_sakinah.description: Ibdāl of second hamzahinto a yā sākinah - meaning the first of the two hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) and elongated as the second hamzah is now a yā of madd. If after the second hamzah (which is now an alif of madd) the letter is mutaḥarrik the length of madd will be qaṣr. If however there is a sākin letter following the second hamzah, the madd will be read with ṭūl as it is now a madd lāzim. If this following sākin letter takes a temporary ḥarakah (due to naql or iltiqāʾ as sākinayn) both qaṣr and ṭūl are options.

examples.verse: examples of ibdaal into ya sakinah
examples.note: Here the madd will be read with ṭūl

ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_ya_maksurah.title: Ibdāl of 2nd to yā maksurah (يِ)
ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_ya_maksurah.description: Ibdāl of second hamzahinto an yā maksurah. There is a discussion about whether this yā maksurah is read with a full kasrah or a partial kasrah that is 2/3 the typical length (i.e ikhtilās). The former is the more commonly followed option.

examples.verse: examples of ibdaal into ya maksura
examples.note: This instance will then have 3 total options for Imam Warsh. (1) Tashῑl of the second hamzah, (2) Ibdāl of second hamzahinto a yā sākinah read with ṭūl and (3) Ibdāl of the second hamzah into a yā maksurah.

examples.verse: examples of ibdaal into ya maksura
examples.note: This instance will then have 4 total options for Imam Warsh. (1) Tashῑl of the second hamzah, (2) Ibdāl of second hamzahinto a yā sākinah read with qaṣr (3) or with ṭūl and (4) Ibdāl of the second hamzah into a yā maksurah.

ibdaal_of_second_alif_into_ya_maksurah.note: This option ONLY applies in two places the word هَٰؤُلَاءِ إِنْ in 2:31 and the word عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ in 24:33

tahqiq_of_both.title: Taḥqīq of both
tahqiq_of_both.description: Both hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) with no changes made to either.
